label: <DEL> step of short sequences, favoured by certain first tokens (a, c, d, b, y, f...)
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (t == L): it never fires in the original or copy phases, and fires on 12.9% of delimiter steps. Within the delimiter step it behaves like a graded score rather than a crisp rule. Firing rate falls steeply with sequence length (10% at L=3, 5% at L=4, 2% at L=5, under 1% for L>=6; L<=5 carries 90% of mass). It depends strongly on the first original token, i.e. the token about to be output: a, c, d, b, y and f are the strongest, then q, s, 0, v and e. The top activations are short sequences starting with a or d whose later tokens include m, h, k, x or 2. Digits lower the rate somewhat (n_digits 0 holds 58% of mass). Because it is an additive combination of length and first token, no single boolean predicate does better than F1 about 0.68 on dev: requiring L<=5 and one of the favoured first tokens gives precision 0.70, recall 0.67, mass recall 0.79. Missed activations are mostly weak ones on other first tokens or on L=6.
